    },

      "name": "flavor_intensity_balance",
      "role": "predictor",

      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,

    },
    {
      "name": "product_effectiveness",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Well-separated categories (works_as_claimed, partially_effective, no_effect, adverse_effect) capturing a distinct product attribute; a strong, interpretable candidate driver of satisfaction."
    },
    {
      "name": "repeat_purchase_intent",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Categories are interpretable, but repurchase intent is essentially an outcome/proxy of satisfaction rather than an external product attribute. Correlating it with satisfaction is near-tautological, not an informative attribute-level relationship, and it is heavily NULL (~46%)."

    }

  "rationale": "Most columns are external, interpretable, well-separated categorical attributes that a human can group on and compare against satisfaction, directly serving the 'what attributes drive satisfaction' query (product_category, flavor_taste_quality, flavor_intensity_balance, product_effectiveness are strong). repeat_purchase_intent is a satisfaction proxy/outcome rather than an attribute, so it partly restates the focus. Several columns carry substantial NULL/not_applicable mass, which limits comparison in subsets, but no column is opaque or a bare score. As a set, the columns support solid interpretable relationship discovery."
